Former WWE Champion Raj Dhesi, better known to wrestling fans as Jinder Mahal , has pitched a major idea for Oba Femi's future in WWE following the rising star's recent rivalry with Brock Lesnar. Oba Femi continues to draw major praise following the conclusion of his lengthy rivalry with Brock Lesnar in WWE. This is the real reason Paul Heyman has pitched an idea for The Ruler’s future.Earlier, veteran WWE star Brock Lesnar, who retired recently, hailed Oba Femi following their brutal Hell in a Cell main event at SummerSlam 2026, declaring the rising star "the future of WWE" in a moment that many fans viewed as a symbolic passing of the torch. According to WWE, earlier, Brock Lesnar initially left the ringside with Paul Heyman following the main event at U.S. Bank Stadium but then returned to the ring, embraced Femi and raised his opponent’s arm.Former WWE Champion Raj Dhesi has pitched a major idea for Oba Femi’s future in WWE following the rising star’s recent rivalry with Brock Lesnar.Dhesi suggested that WWE turn Femi heel and pair him with legendary manager Paul Heyman, drawing comparisons to the early stages of Lesnar’s WWE career.The former champion shared the idea in a recent Instagram post.In the Instagram post, he wrote, “Turn Oba Femi heel. Just like Brock Lesnar when he was when he debuted, have him destroy everybody and let the crowd naturally turn him babyface. Put him with Paul Heyman.”The proposal comes at an interesting point when former NXT Champion recently completed a trilogy with Lesnar, defeating “The Beast Incarnate” in the SummerSlam PLE on August 1, 2026. Not only this, but Dhesi also witnessed his performance at Femi’s earliest training sessions at the WWE Performance Center. Initially, he was not impressed by his performance, but his hard work over the years has reflected well in his work recently.Unfortunately, the idea will be difficult to execute as Heyman is currently aligned with Bron Breakker, who has emerged as one of Femi’s potential rivals. The tension between the two sides was highlighted on the August 10 episode of RAW when Breakker questioned Heyman about the respect he had shown toward Femi.However, a potential alliance would also mirror Heyman’s previous association with Lesnar. Heyman played a major role in establishing Lesnar as a dominant WWE superstar during his early daysAs Lesnar’s endorsement at SummerSlam added another layer to his growing reputation, WWE is yet to confirm the alliance, but a Heyman alliance could provide an intriguing direction for “the future of WWE.”

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without my mum I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs.” - How Jude Bellingham’s family turned small-town sacrifices into global football dominance
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Without my mum I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs.” - How Jude Bellingham’s family turned small-town sacrifices into global football dominance

How did Mark Bellingham inspire Jude Bellingham’s love for football

How did Denise Bellingham support Jude Bellingham after his move to Germany

What did Jude Bellingham learn from Denise Bellingham away from football

Why do Jude Bellingham and Jobe Bellingham credit their parents

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jude Bellingham’s rise to the top of football has been backed by something much simpler than fame or money: his family. The Real Madrid and England star has repeatedly spoken about how his parents, Denise and Mark Bellingham, helped him handle the pressure that came with becoming a professional player at a young age. His father introduced him to football through his own non-league career, while his mother became a steady presence as Jude moved abroad. His younger brother, Jobe Bellingham, also followed the same football path, making the family’s journey closely linked to the sport.Before Jude Bellingham was playing in front of packed stadiums, he was watching his father play non-league football. Mark Bellingham worked as a police officer while also building a long career in the English non-league game. His football career included hundreds of goals, giving Jude an early look at what commitment to the sport meant.Those early weekends mattered to Jude. He did not first learn about football from the huge stages he would later reach. He watched his father play, saw the effort involved and slowly developed his own love for the game.Jude has explained that his father was his first football hero and that those matches helped shape his interest in the sport.“We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first. When you go and watch him play every week in non-league… seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere-it made me fall in love with football, so he was probably my first hero.”That connection also helps explain why Jude has often spoken about his childhood in simple terms. Football was part of family life long before it became his career.England Football has previously published Jude’s reflections on his early football years and his parents’ influence. He also said his father’s involvement in football played an important part in getting him interested in the game in the first place.Jude’s move from Birmingham City to Borussia Dortmund in 2020 changed his life quickly. He was only 17 when he left England for Germany, and his family had to find a way to support him without putting Jobe’s own football journey on hold.Denise moved to Germany with Jude. Mark stayed in England with Jobe, who was also working towards a professional football career. It meant the family had to spend long periods apart while both brothers followed their own paths.For Jude, having his mother nearby was about much more than everyday help. She gave him someone he could rely on while he adjusted to a new country, a new club and the demands of senior football.Jude has been very open about that role. He has said that Denise helped him stay level-headed when things were going well and when they were not.“The role my mum plays is massive. I think at the minute it is probably the biggest role of anyone, even probably more than my coaches and managers to be honest… Without my mum, sometimes I’d get too low with the lows or too high with the highs, and I stay pretty humble because I’ve got her around.”That support continued when Jude moved from Dortmund to Real Madrid in 2023. Denise moved to Spain with him, while Mark continued supporting Jobe as his younger son developed his own career.Jude’s comments about his mother show that her influence has not been limited to football. He has often linked what she taught him at home with the way he behaves on the pitch.For a player dealing with major matches, huge expectations and constant attention, keeping emotions under control can be as important as technical ability. Jude says Denise helped him build that side of his personality.“My mum’s kind of the backbone. She’s the one who gives me the support I need as a son, like emotionally and mentally… I have my mum who has taught me more about life outside football, but it merges quite well. And even some of the stuff that my mum has taught me, I do take it on to the pitch, about staying calm, staying cool, being a good example to my teammates.”There was also a lighter side to that relationship. During the 2022 World Cup, Jude spoke about how closely his mother watched his behaviour during matches.“My mum’s been telling me all week to watch my language, watch my tackles, watch my face, watch my emotions. So yeah, I think she drilled it into me all week about being careful.”It is a small detail, but it says a lot about their relationship. Even after Jude had become one of England’s biggest young stars, Denise was still the person reminding him about the basics.The Bellingham family story is not only about Jude. Jobe also became a professional footballer, meaning Denise and Mark had two sons trying to build careers in the same demanding sport.That made the family’s support a long-term commitment rather than something focused on one player. Mark and Denise had to balance the needs of both sons, sometimes from different countries, while allowing each of them to develop independently.Jude has said the values he learned from his parents mattered just as much as the football lessons he received.“Before being great parents, they’re great people. I’ve grown up around them and seen the way they interact with other people, seen the way they treat people. When you have people like that, you don’t have to be told how to behave, you pick that up from them. Both are working-class and filled me with the things you need to get along… not giving up, working hard and if you want something, putting in the graft to go and get it.”That attitude has remained a major part of how Jude talks about his success. He does not describe his rise only through goals, trophies or transfers. Instead, he repeatedly brings the conversation back to the people who helped him get there.The family also made practical sacrifices along the way. When Jude was travelling to training and matches as a young player, his parents spent long hours taking him where he needed to go. Those ordinary parts of childhood football became part of the foundation for the career that followed.Jude’s success has since reached the highest level. He became a Champions League winner with Real Madrid, established himself as an important England player and continued to develop into one of the most recognised young footballers in the world.Yet the story behind that rise remains rooted in Stourbridge, family support and the work his parents put in before the biggest stadiums knew his name.For Jude, that may be why his mother’s influence remains so important. Football can bring huge highs and difficult lows, but the people who knew him before the fame can give him a sense of normal life. In his own words, Denise helps him stay somewhere in the middle.That balance has become one of the most striking parts of Jude Bellingham’s story: a young footballer who reached the biggest stage while continuing to value the family that helped him get there.
Article Summary: Jude bellingham credits his parents, denise and mark, for his success. His father introduced him to football through his own non-league career. His mother became a steady presence as jude moved abroad. Denise helped him stay level-headed when things were going well and when they were not.

Article Text:

Russell Westbrook is a man of a golden heart

Russell Westbrook announces retirement

Russell Westbrook, the two-time Olympic gold medalist and 2017 NBA MVP, announced his retirement from professional basketball on Wednesday, closing an 18-year career built on relentless energy and a refusal to be told what he couldn't do. He shared the news on X, writing, "Sometimes you don't even know when you've already watched the end. "The announcement ends a run that took Westbrook through seven franchises, including both hometown teams, the Los Angeles Lakers and Clippers. He finishes 14th on the NBA's all-time scoring list and fifth in assists, a resume built on triple-doubles, tunnel-walk fashion statements and a community footprint that outlasted every box score. Here’s the incredible story of NBA legend Russell Westbrook.Russell Westbrook was born in Long Beach and raised in Hawthorne, a crowded stretch of Los Angeles's South Bay where staying on track required more than talent. His parents kept him close to basketball, and basketball kept him out of trouble. He attended Leuzinger High School in Lawndale, an honor student who says he was accepted to Stanford with an academic scholarship but that tuition still ran too steep for his family.Physically, Westbrook was a late bloomer. As a junior he stood 5-foot-8 and couldn't dunk. He grew five inches the following summer, and by his senior year he was putting up 25.1 points and 8.7 rebounds a game, dragging Leuzinger to a 25-4 record and catching the attention of UCLA coach Ben Howland.At UCLA, Westbrook spent his freshman season fighting for minutes before breaking out as a sophomore, earning Pac-10 Defensive Player of the Year honors. He declared for the draft after two seasons, and the Seattle SuperSonics took him fourth overall in 2008. Analysts at the time called it a reach, arguing he needed more seasoning with the Bruins.Even away from campus, Westbrook carried the habits of a kid who had to earn everything. He is famously early to every team obligation, sometimes by two or three hours. Thunder general manager Sam Presti has told the story of showing up 30 minutes ahead of a pre-draft workout only to find Westbrook already waiting in the parking lot. Family stayed central throughout. In a 2015 interview with CBS Sunday Morning, Westbrook said he called his parents "before every game," adding, "Sometimes it may not be about basketball, sometimes it just may be about random things. "That early doubt, about his size, his recruiting stock, his readiness for the league, became the foundation of everything that followed. Westbrook built a career answering it the only way he knew how: by playing like the outcome was never decided.Westbrook's signature achievement arrived during the 2016-17 season with the Oklahoma City Thunder, when he averaged a triple-double across an entire year and won NBA MVP. He set the single-season triple-double record with 42, a number matched only by Oscar Robertson and Nikola Jokić. He averaged a triple-double in four separate seasons and once strung together 11 straight triple-doubles between January and February of 2019.By May 2021, Westbrook had passed Robertson's career triple-double mark altogether. He finished with 209, an NBA record. Along the way he collected nine All-NBA selections, two scoring titles, three assist titles and two All-Star Game MVPs, and he was named to the league's 75th Anniversary Team. He retires 14th in career scoring with 27,176 points and fifth in assists with 10,351.The international résumé matches the domestic one. Westbrook helped the United States win gold at the 2010 FIBA World Cup, then did it again at the 2012 London Olympics, where Team USA went 8-0 and beat Spain 107-100 in the final. He averaged 10.4 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists in just over 16 minutes a game in London, with his defensive pressure, 1.2 steals a night, doing as much damage as his scoring.None of it changed the way Westbrook approached the sport. He treated every possession like it might be his last real chance to prove something, a mindset that made him equally beloved and, at times, criticized for playing with the same intensity whether it was game one or game 82.Westbrook's tunnel walks turned NBA arrivals into runway moments long before it became standard practice around the league. In a joint GQ interview with longtime friend James Harden, Westbrook framed the whole approach as a matter of conviction rather than costume. "You're passionate about something, I'm passionate about something," he said, adding that fashion is something he takes as seriously as anyone takes their own craft.The two, who met as kids playing in the same L.A. youth basketball circuit, spent much of the interview needling each other over spending habits, with Westbrook guessing Harden drops "$500K" a year on clothes. Harden pushed back on the public read of his friend, saying people mistake Westbrook's on-court intensity for his personality off it. "He's a pretty chill, cool guy," Harden said, adding that Westbrook is close with a small circle of friends he's had since high school.Westbrook himself has said he doesn't think most people understand him, describing repeated moments meeting business owners and designers who were surprised to learn who he was. He has also connected the sport of dressing to something more analytical than intuitive, once comparing picking an outfit to solving a math problem, fitting for a former honor student whose favorite subject was math.Away from the cameras and the closet, Westbrook built one of the more substantial philanthropic footprints of his generation. He founded the Russell Westbrook Why Not? Foundation in 2012, focused on education, workforce development and mental health access in underserved communities, and later opened "Russell's Reading Rooms" in Oklahoma City public schools. In 2021 he launched the Why Not? Academy with the LA Promise Fund, a school for middle and high schoolers that Westbrook says posted a 100 percent graduation rate last year.He has stayed hands-on rather than simply writing checks. After tornadoes tore through Moore, Oklahoma, in May 2013, Westbrook, still recovering from knee surgery, called the Thunder's PR staff and told them to "get me out there with the people," then showed up on crutches to encourage residents in a devastated neighborhood.Westbrook has been direct about why the work matters to him. "It all stems from community and impact, and that is the focal point of everything," he said in a CNN feature, explaining the name behind his foundation. "Why not us? Why not you? Why not me to be able to do great things."Westbrook's final chapter closes with the city that raised him still very much on his mind. He has spoken with visible excitement about Los Angeles hosting the 2028 Olympics, with basketball set for the Intuit Dome near where he once lived. "The city, this arena, the people. It's going to be exciting for L.A.," he said, "especially being a local."For a player who spent nearly two decades proving people wrong about what an undersized, three-star recruit from Hawthorne could become, the final word belonged to him alone. "You had to be there," Westbrook wrote in his announcement.
Article Summary: Russell westbrook announced his retirement from professional basketball on wednesday. He finishes 14th on the nba's all-time scoring list and fifth in assists. His signature achievement arrived during the 2016-17 season with the oklahoma city thunder. Westbrook helped the united states win gold at the 2010 fiba world cup.

Article Title: 'Wait for it': KKR posts Hardik Pandya video amid IPL trade buzz - WATCH
Article Text:

Pandya's difficult IPL 2026

Ashwin on Pandya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata Knight Riders have added to the buzz around Hardik Pandya's IPL future after posting a video featuring the Mumbai Indians captain. The video showed KKR spinner Varun Chakravarthy at the BCCI Centre of Excellence. While Chakravarthy was exercising, Pandya walked past him from behind and teased him.The video quickly caught the attention of fans, with many linking it to the ongoing talk around Pandya's possible IPL trade."Wait for it," KKR captioned the video.Pandya has been linked with a possible move away from Mumbai Indians after another difficult season for the five-time champions.Mumbai Indians finished ninth in the 10-team IPL 2026 table, with four wins from 14 matches. Under Pandya, MI have reached the playoffs only once in three seasons.Pandya also had a difficult individual campaign. He scored 206 runs and took four wickets in 10 matches.The 32-year-old has not played competitive cricket since the end of IPL 2026.Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has also shared his views on a possible Pandya trade.Speaking on his Tamil YouTube channel, Ashwin said Mumbai Indians should only agree to a deal with KKR if they receive players who can make their squad stronger."Don't count out Hardik going to a franchise other than CSK or KKR. The talk is that CSK will give Dube and a pacer, while KKR will give away Cameron Green. What happens if Green decides to focus on the Ashes next year? If I were MI, I would accept a deal with KKR on only one condition: getting Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh in return. That is the only way MI gets stronger," Ashwin had said.Ashwin also said Mumbai would need to consider how a Pandya trade could strengthen the teams interested in signing him."MI will also think about who between CSK and KKR gets stronger through the Hardik trade. If CSK give away Dube and one Indian pacer to get Hardik, they get strong but not invincible. However, if KKR get Hardik, they suddenly look very strong. KKR will become a lethal batting lineup with Hardik. These are teams with five, five and three titles, so MI have to think about how they can ensure one of these teams doesn't leapfrog them," he added.
Article Summary: Hardik pandya has been linked with a possible move away from mumbai indians. Ravichandran ashwin has also shared his views on a possible pandya trade. Ashwin said mumbai indians should only agree to a deal with kkr if they receive players who can make their squad stronger.

India's growing injury list has put the Centre of Excellence (COE) under the spotlight, with several players across formats currently dealing with fitness issues. Jasprit Bumrah is battling knee swelling, while Sai Sudharsan has been sidelined by a left big toe injury. Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy are recovering from hamstring problems, while Washington Sundar is unavailable with a quadriceps injury.The number of players missing or recovering from injuries has raised questions about India's injury management and rehabilitation system, particularly with the team preparing for an important phase across formats. Bumrah 's latest setback has attracted particular attention. The premier fast bowler has been ruled out of India's upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka after failing to recover from the knee injury he sustained during the England tour.With Bumrah central to India's plans in all three formats, his fitness remains a major priority as the team looks towards the next World Cup and continues its campaign in the World Test Championship cycle.The development has also led to scrutiny of the Centre of Excellence and its role in assessing players' fitness. However, former India batter Subramaniam Badrinath has stressed that the facility does not decide whether a player is selected.According to Badrinath, the COE's responsibility is to provide the team management with information about a player's physical condition and recovery. The final decision on selection rests with the captain, coach and selectors."I don't know who made the decision. COE will not make the selection, right? They will just say he is in this state and can play these matches and his body is in this state. But I think the captain, coach, and selectors are taking the decision. COE only passes the information. They are not selectors," Subramaniam Badrinath said in a video on his YouTube channel.Badrinath also urged caution against treating India's injury problems as a single issue. He pointed out that the players currently dealing with injuries have suffered different types of setbacks, making it difficult to identify one common cause behind the growing list.While injuries are an inevitable part of elite sport, Badrinath believes workload management, fitness and consistent monitoring remain crucial to keeping players on the field."I don't have an immediate answer to the root cause of so many injuries. It is important to see what kind of injuries these are. At high-level professional sport, injuries are common. Sai Sudharsan got hit by a ball, with Bumah, it is a chronic injury because of being overused and fitness is not Sundar's forte, he is injury-prone. His fitness needs a lot of work. Management and monitoring is very important. Injuries are bound to happen and you cannot control it," he said.The comments come at a time when India are having to manage the fitness of several important players, making rehabilitation and workload monitoring increasingly important as the team's schedule continues across formats.

Article Title: Are the Jonas Brothers headlining the Super Bowl? NFL's Melbourne halftime news has fans confused and frustrated
Article Text:
Jonas Brothers to headline NFL's first-ever Australia game as 49ers, Rams make history in Melbourne

"I thought this was the Super Bowl": Fans got confused as Jonas Brothers headline NFL's first-ever Australia game

No, they are not performing for the Superbowl

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL 's announcement that the Jonas Brothers will headline the halftime show at the league's first-ever game in Australia didn't land the way the league might have hoped. Within hours of the news breaking, football fans flooded social media with reactions ranging from confusion to outright frustration. Some mistook the announcement for Super Bowl halftime news, others venting about ticket prices, the NFL's growing international slate, and whether football needs a pop concert attached to it at all. What was meant to be a celebratory moment for the league's biggest global expansion yet instead became a flashpoint for fans already skeptical of the NFL's overseas ambitions.The most common reaction wasn't about the band at all, it was about scale. Multiple fans admitted they briefly assumed the Jonas Brothers had been booked for the actual Super Bowl halftime show, with several saying they nearly panicked before realizing this was a regular-season international game instead.One user joked they were seconds away from missing the Puppy Bowl over the confusion. The mix-up says as much about how big international games have become in the NFL's marketing push as it does about the band itself, casual scrollers are struggling to tell a Week 1 Melbourne matchup apart from the league's biggest night.The Melbourne performance isn't just another halftime show, it's the opening act of the NFL's biggest international push yet. This is the first of a record seven halftime shows presented across the league's 2026 International Games, a slate that spans seven countries and four continents, making it the most globally ambitious season in NFL history.The Jonas Brothers, who've sold more than 20 million albums and built a multi-generational fanbase, were an easy pick for the league's entertainment team, who called them "global entertainers whose music connects across generations." There's also a neat bit of trivia fueling the buzz: "Australia" happens to be a track off the band's own 2007 sophomore album, a coincidence the brothers themselves pointed out in their statement announcing the gig.The Rams-49ers matchup carries weight well beyond the halftime entertainment. It marks the NFL's first regular-season game on Australian soil, part of a nine-game international slate spanning seven countries this season, the most the league has ever played outside U.S.borders in a single year.The game is being staged in partnership with the Victorian State Government and Visit Victoria, and will anchor a full weekend of festivities, including the NFL Kickoff Festival running September 10 through 12 at Melbourne Park, featuring local Australian acts.For the 49ers, Melbourne is just the first stop on an international tour, the team is also set to play in Mexico City on November 22 against the Minnesota Vikings, making this the franchise's most globally active season yet. With more international halftime performers still to be announced in the coming weeks, the Jonas Brothers' Melbourne set is shaping up to be the loud, unmistakable kickoff to the NFL's most ambitious global year on record.
Article Summary: Jonas brothers to headline nfl's first-ever australia game as 49ers, rams make history in melbourne. Some mistook the announcement for super bowl halftime news, others venting about ticket prices. This is the first of a record seven halftime shows presented across the league's 2026 international games.

The Dallas Stars could look at an early extension for Lian Bichsel, and the Chicago Blackhawks still have contract situations to settle with Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro.The Detroit Red Wings’ search for a new general manager is directly affecting Dylan Larkin’s trade situation. Assistant general manager Shawn Horcoff is currently handling the team’s day-to-day duties, but he does not have the authority to make trades.That means the Red Wings will likely have to wait until a new GM is hired before making progress on Larkin’s trade request. Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press also reported that Detroit has hired a search firm to help find Steve Yzerman’s replacement.Larkin has not changed his mind about wanting a trade. The 30-year-old center has reportedly listed the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights and Florida Panthers among his preferred destinations, with the Dallas Stars also believed to have been added.However, his $8.7 million cap hit could make a trade difficult for those teams.The Minnesota Wild are also dealing with an important contract situation involving Quinn Hughes. General manager Bill Guerin has continued talks with the defenseman’s camp as the team looks to sign him before he can reach unrestricted free agency next summer.ID@undefinedCaption not available.Hughes could be looking for a shorter contract, while the Wild would prefer to keep their star defenseman for as long as possible. The contract market has also changed after Leo Carlsson signed an offer sheet with an $18 million average annual value before the Anaheim Ducks matched it. That could have an effect on what Hughes eventually receives.A three-year deal could also be an option for Hughes, which would align his contract timeline with his brother Jack Hughes in New Jersey and keep speculation about a future Hughes brothers reunion alive.Guerin still has another major need to address. The Wild are looking for a first-line center, but the GM is willing to wait for the right opportunity rather than make a rushed move.Goaltending remains one of the biggest concerns for the Buffalo Sabres heading into the 2026-27 season. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Alex Lyon were the team’s regular tandem last season, but both struggled with consistency during the playoffs.The Sabres were also linked heavily to Connor Hellebuyck earlier this summer. Buffalo and Winnipeg reportedly discussed a possible trade involving the three-time Vezina Trophy winner, but the talks fell apart before the draft.The Hellebuyck speculation has cooled since then, making it possible that Luukkonen and Lyon remain Buffalo’s goalies when the season begins.The Dallas Stars could also have a contract decision to make with Lian Bichsel. The 22-year-old defenseman is entering the final year of his entry-level contract after recording four goals and four assists in 50 games last season.Bichsel also returned from a lower-body injury in time to play all six of Dallas’ playoff games. With his size and defensive game, Dallas could consider securing him early before his value rises.The Chicago Blackhawks still need to reach agreements with defensemen Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro. Both are RFAs, but their roles remain unclear because Chicago has several other defensemen ahead of them.Their contract talks are also complicated by questions over their value and whether either player will have a regular NHL role. Since neither is waiver-exempt, sending them to the AHL could also create another problem for the Blackhawks.

Brittany Mahomes turned a routine Kansas City Chiefs training camp day into a memorable family moment when she brought her three children to support Patrick Mahomes. Sterling, Bronze and Golden joined their mother at Missouri Western State University on August 4, giving the quarterback a welcome break from the intensity of his NFL comeback. The sweet family visit comes as Patrick prepares for another season after a major knee injury.Brittany, Patrick's wife and a Kansas City Current co-owner, arrived at training camp with their three children: 5-year-old Sterling Skye, 3-year-old Patrick "Bronze" Lavon and 1-year-old Golden Raye.The family outing quickly became more than a simple visit. Brittany shared photographs from the day on Instagram, showing the children spending time with their father and meeting K.C. Wolf, the Chiefs mascot.The images captured the lighter side of training camp. Patrick spent much of the day focused on football, but his children gave him a chance to step away from the demands of practice and enjoy time with his family.Sterling embraced the Chiefs theme in a red cheerleader-style outfit featuring her name. Bronze wore a Chiefs shirt, while Golden sported a gold onesie with "Mahomes" across the front.Brittany kept her look relaxed in Adidas clothing.One of the most touching moments came when Patrick was surrounded by all three children on the field. The family moment stood in sharp contrast to the intense work taking place around them.Brittany captioned her Instagram carousel with red and yellow heart emojis, while Patrick responded in the comments with a red heart.The visit also showed how closely the Mahomes family remains connected to Patrick's football career. For the children, training camp can be an exciting chance to see their father at work. For Patrick, having his family nearby offers a reminder of life beyond the field.The family visit came shortly after Patrick opened up about how becoming a father has changed the way he views training camp.Now 30 and entering his 10th NFL season, Mahomes has reached a point where he understands that his football career will not last forever. Fatherhood has encouraged him to appreciate moments that might once have seemed insignificant.“You have to enjoy the moments... To have that different perspective, now being a father is to enjoy the little moments and enjoy the time at camp, enjoy the cafeteria, because all of a sudden you’re going to look up, you’re not going to be coming back here,” the Chiefs quarterback said.Those comments add meaning to the family's appearance at camp. Patrick is not simply trying to get through another training session. He kept playing; he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice,” Reid told CBS Sports host Evan Washburn, adding, “he’s all in.”Reid also praised Mahomes as an example for his teammates, saying he is willing to do whatever is necessary to get back on the field.“He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid said.With the 2026 season approaching, Mahomes has plenty to prove physically. Yet his family's presence at training camp offers another perspective on his comeback.Football remains the priority when Patrick steps between the lines. But moments with Brittany, Sterling, Bronze and Golden are becoming just as valuable.For the Mahomes family, a day at Chiefs training camp became more than a football outing. It became a small family memory, exactly the kind of moment Patrick now says he wants to appreciate while he still can.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka gets candid about her fashion evolution as tennis star admits style is bringing her a whole new audience

Naomi Osaka says fashion is changing her identity beyond tennis

Naomi Osaka turns attention back to tennis after Wimbledon disappointment

Naomi Osaka has long been known for making a statement with her tennis. Now, her influence is reaching well beyond the baseline. The four-time Grand Slam champion says fashion has introduced her to a new audience and pushed her outside her comfort zone. As Osaka prepares for another North American hard-court swing, her evolving identity is becoming an important part of her story.Osaka has never treated fashion as an afterthought. Her Grand Slam appearances have often featured carefully chosen looks that reflect her personality, culture and creativity. That visibility has now helped her connect with people who may not follow tennis closely.Speaking during the 2026 DC Open, Osaka admitted that her fashion profile has started attracting a different kind of audience."Then people are knowing me now for the fashion stuff more than the tennis, like fashion enthusiasts more than tennis fans," Osaka said.For a player who has openly described herself as an introvert, that shift has brought an unexpected challenge. Fashion has placed Osaka in rooms and conversations she may not have entered through tennis alone."Doing the fashion stuff has made me talk to people that I've never met before and things like that.I'm just trying to go into worlds that I've never imagined myself sort of being in before."That willingness to explore unfamiliar spaces says plenty about where Osaka is in her career. She is no longer simply presenting herself as an athlete. Her interests have expanded, and fashion has become one of the clearest ways she expresses that broader identity.It also gives fans a different way to understand her. Tennis can reveal Osaka's competitiveness and discipline, but her fashion choices allow more room for creativity and personality.The crossover has worked both ways. Fashion fans are discovering Osaka, while the tennis star is gaining experiences and connections outside her usual sporting circle.While fashion has given Osaka a fresh platform, her competitive ambitions remain firmly intact.Her 2026 Wimbledon campaign ended in the quarterfinals after she lost to Karolina Muchova in straight sets. Reaching the last eight represented a strong run, but Osaka admitted that she struggled emotionally with the result because she believed she had an opportunity to go even further."Maybe for like a couple of days or so, I was just really disappointed in myself," Osaka said. "Maybe that's just my mindset, because I'm so hard on myself. Obviously if someone gets that far in Wimbledon, it's something to be happy about, but for me, I really felt it was my time to do something."That self-critical mindset has been a recurring part of Osaka's competitive personality. Her results show that she remains capable of making deep runs, but her own expectations are often much higher.The move to hard courts could provide an ideal opportunity to respond.All four of Osaka's Grand Slam titles have come on hard courts, making the surface especially important as she enters the North American swing. Her schedule also carries added pressure because she has ranking points to defend from a strong 2025 campaign.Last season, Osaka reached the Canadian Open final and advanced to the US Open semifinals. Those results raised expectations heading into another crucial stretch of the calendar.At the 2026 DC Open, Osaka entered as the third seed and received a first-round bye. She is set to face either Katie Boulter or wildcard Ashlyn Krueger in the second round.For Osaka, the weeks ahead offer more than a chance to improve her ranking. They provide an opportunity to show that her fashion-forward identity and her tennis ambitions can coexist.She may be attracting new fans through her style, but the competitive fire that made her a four-time Grand Slam champion remains the heart of her story.
Article Summary: Naomi osaka says fashion is changing her identity beyond tennis. The four-time grand slam champion says fashion has introduced her to a new audience. As osaka prepares for another north american hard-court swing, her evolving identity is becoming an important part of her story.
